So, you finally climbed Olympus Mons. Most travellers see the height, hear the wind, and turn back before they ever find my door. You kept coming. That tells me more about you than the markings on your suit.
Khazglar. That is the name you may call me. I live up here because the mountain gives a craftsman something the settlements never could: quiet enough to hear what a damaged engine is trying to say.

And yours has plenty to say. Dust in the seams, scorch marks along the hull, a coating of half the worlds you have visited. I can make your ship nice and clean, traveller. Under all that grime, there is still a fine vessel waiting to be seen.

Cleaning is more than polishing metal until it shines. A blocked intake can starve a drive, and grit beneath a seal can ruin a journey. Before I trust a ship to carry someone into the dark, I want every plate, vent, and fastening in order.

You have travelled farther than that old engine was ever meant to take you comfortably. I imagine you have spent a fair amount of time staring at a distant world and wishing it would hurry towards you. There are better ways to cross that distance.

I can help you get a faster ship. Whether we improve the one you brought or eventually find you a better hull, speed begins with understanding the machine. A powerful engine on a poorly prepared vessel is only an expensive way to come apart.

Start with the propulsion system. Stronger drive assemblies, properly balanced power delivery, and sound thermal control will let you travel faster without sacrificing everything that keeps you alive. Gather the right supplies, and put them towards your ship's drive upgrades.

Do not mistake speed for invulnerability. An asteroid does not care how magnificent your new engines are, and a star will burn a careless pilot just as readily as a brave one. Keep your hull repaired and leave yourself room to slow down.

Bring your ship to a clear landing site when you return. Keep its systems in good order, collect useful materials on your travels, and come back with a plan for the journeys ahead. I would rather help you build something dependable than watch you chase a promise that fails halfway home.

There. You found the old craftsman above the clouds, and now you know what I can offer: a ship you can take pride in, and a path towards something faster. Rest a moment, traveller. The stars will still be waiting when you are ready to leave.
